2000.lxx: in LXX for כָּרַת, שָׁחַת hi., etc.
2000.full: ὀλοθρεύω (ὄλεθρος), late (Alex.) form of ὄλεθρεύω ω (cf. MGr., ξολοθρεύω) [in LXX for כָּרַת, שָׁחַת hi., etc. ;] to destroy: Heb.11:28 (cf. ἐξ-ολοθρεύω).† ὀλεθρεύω, see: ὀλοθρεύω ὀλοθρεύω (ὄλεθρος), late (Alex.) form of ὄλεθρεύω ω (cf. MGr., ξολοθρεύω) [in LXX for כָּרַת, שָׁחַת hi., etc. ;] to destroy: Heb.11:28 (cf. ἐξ-ολοθρεύω).† ὀλεθρεύω, see: ὀλοθρεύω (AS)

2001.full: a hoof, the solid hoof of the horse and ass, (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;after (Homer), like χηλή, the cloven hoof of horned cattle, (Homeric Hymns), etc. (ML)

2002.full: 1. a marking out by boundaries, limitation , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. the definition of a word , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

2003.full: ὑδρία, -ας, ἠ (ὕδωρ), [in LXX for בַּד ;] __1. prop., a water-pot or jar: Jhn.2:6, 7 John 4:28. __2. More frequently in Attic = ἄγγυς, a pot, urn or jar of any kind, as for holding wine, coins, etc. (see Rutherford, NPhr., 23; MM, xxv). † (AS)

2004.lxx: in LXX for אַחֲרוֹן and cogn. forms
2004.full: ὕστερος, -α, -ον [in LXX for אַחֲרוֹן and cogn. forms ;] latter, later: ἐν ὑ. καιροῖς, 1Ti.4:1 (on the reading ὁ ὕ., WH, for ὁ πρῶτος, see WH, App., in l). Neut., τὸ ὕ., used adverbially instead of ὑστέρως, afterwards, later: Mat.4:2 21:29, 32 21:37 25:11 26:60, Mrk.16:14, Luk.20:32, Jhn.13:36, Heb.12:11; with genitive, Mat.22:27.† (AS)

2005.full: 1. the pangs or throes of labour, travail-pains , (Iliad by Homer); ἐν μόναις ὠδῖσιν at a single birth , (Pindar); ἐν ὠδίνων ἀνάγκαις (Euripides); in singular travail-pain, anguish , (Pindar) 2. in singular, also, the fruit of travail or labour, a birth, child , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἄπτερον ὠδῖνα τέκνων, of young birds, (Euripides) 3. metaphorically any travail, anguish , (Aeschulus Tragicus); also in plural, of love, pangs , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

2006.full: Καίν (Τ, Κάϊν), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Κάϊς, -ιος), (Heb. קַיִן; Gen.4:1), Cain: Heb.11:4, 1Jn.3:12, Ju 11.† (AS)

2010.full: βελτίων, -ον (genitive -ονος), comp. of ἀγαθός, [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;] neut. as adv., better, very well: 2Ti.1:18 (also Act.10:28 D). On elative use in these passages, see M, Pr., 78, 236.† (AS)

2012.full: γονεύς, -έως, ὁ (γίγνομαι), [in LXX for אָב, אֵם ;] a begetter, a father; mostly in pl., οἱ γ., parents: Luk.2:41, 43 8:56 21:16, Jhn.9:2, 3 20, 22, 23 Rom.1:30, 2Co.12:14, Eph.6:1, Col.3:20, 2Ti.3:2; accusative pl. (Hellenistic, see Thackeray, Gr., i, 148), γονεῖς, Mat.10:21, Mrk.13:22, Luk.2:27 18:29, Jhn.9:18.† (AS)

s: in OT, heathen deities, false gods
2013.lxx: in LXX (so also in π; see MM, Exp., x) for שֵׁד, אֱלִיל, (frequently in To)
2013.full: δαιμόνιον, -ου, τό (neut. of δαιμόνιος, -α, -ον, divine), [in LXX (so also in π; see MM, Exp., x) for שֵׁד, אֱלִיל, (frequently in To) ;] __1. as in cl.; __(a) the Divine power, Deity (Hdt., Plat., al.); __(b) an inferior divinity, deity or demon (as in magical π, Deiss., BS, 281; MM, Exp., x): ξένα δ., Act.17:18. __2. (a) in OT, heathen deities, false gods (e.g. Deu.32:17, Psa.95 (96):5); __(b) in NT, evil spirits, demons: θύουσιν δαιμονίοις, 1Co.10:20; διδασκαλίαι δαιμονίων, 1Ti.4:1; προσκυνεῖν τὰ δ., Rev.9:20; ἄρχων τῶν δ., Mat.9:34; especially (syn. with πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον) as operating upon and "possessing" (of. δαιμονίζομαι) men: Mat.11:18, and al.; εἰσέρχεσθαι δ. εἰς. . ., Luk.8:30; δ. ἔχειν, Luk.4:33; δ. ἐκβάλλειν, Mat.7:22 In the phrase πνεῦμα δαιμονίου ἀκαθάρτου, Luk.4:33, the wider cl. usage (1. b) is recognised, ἀκ. being elsewhere in NT, the epithet of πν., and δ. = πν. ἀκ. (see ICC, in l; Cremer, 168) (AS)

2014.full: 1. absolute to be lord or master, gain the mastery , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. with genitive to be lord or master of , (Homeric Hymns), etc.; δεσπόζειν φόβης to own the lock of hair, (Aeschulus Tragicus); metaphorically to master , δ. λόγου (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. with accusative to lord it over , (Euripides) (ML)

2016.full: 1. originally a tree (which indeed comes from the same Root), commonly the oak , Lat. quercus, (Homer), etc.; sacred to Zeus, who gave his oracles from the oaks of Dodona, (Odyssey by Homer);—;hence, αἱ προσήγοροι δρύες (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;proverbial, οὐ γὰρ ἀπὸ δρυός ἐσσι οὐδ᾽ ἀπὸ πέτρης thou art no foundling from tree or rock, i. e. thou hast parents and a country, (Odyssey by Homer); οὐ νῦν ἐστιν ἀπὸ δρυὸς οὐδ᾽ ἀπὸ πέτρης ὀαρίζειν 'tis no time now to talk at ease from tree or rock, (Iliad by Homer) 2. of other trees, πίειρα δρῦς the resinous wood (of the pine), (Sophocles Tragicus); of the olive, (Euripides) 3. metaphorically a wornout old man , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

2017.lxx: in LXX for טָהֵר, טׇהֳרָה, etc.
2017.full: καθαρισμός, -oῦ, τό (καθαρίζω). [in LXX for טָהֵר, טׇהֳרָה, etc. ;] cleansing, purification: Jhn.3:25; with genitive subjc., τ. Ἰουδαίων, Jhn.2:6; with genitive obj., of women after childbirth, Luk.2:22; of lepers, Mrk.1:44, Luk.5:14; with genitive of thing(s), τ. ἁμαρτιῶν, Heb.1:3, 2Pe.1:9 (Cremer, 319).† (AS)

2018.lxx: in LXX chiefly for קַשׁ, Exo.5:12, Isa.5:24, al.
2018.full: καλάμη, -ης, ἡ (cf. κάλαμος), [in LXX chiefly for קַשׁ, Exo.5:12, Isa.5:24, al. ;] a stalk of corn, stubble: 1Co.3:12.† (AS)

s: to use concealment, to conceal oneself
2019.full: 1. to cover over, hide away, conceal , (Homer), etc. 2. absolute to use concealment, to conceal oneself , of the gods, (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

2020.lxx: in LXX for מוֹשָׁב, מָעוֹן, etc.
2020.full: κατ-οικητήριον, -ου, τό (κατοικέω), [in LXX for מוֹשָׁב, מָעוֹן, etc. ;] a habitation, dwelling-place: Eph.2:22, Rev.18:2.† (AS)

2021.full: κρίνον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for שׁוּשַׁן ;] a lily: Mat.6:28, Luk.12:27.† (AS)

2022.lxx: in LXX chiefly for כָּרַע, 4Ki.1:13, 2Ch.29:29, Isa.45:24 (23), al.
2022.full: κάμπτω [in LXX chiefly for כָּרַע, 4Ki.1:13, 2Ch.29:29, Isa.45:24 (23), al. ;] to bend, bow: with accusative of thing(s), γόνυ, τὰ γ.; with dative of person(s), τῇ Βάαλ, Rom.11:4 (LXX); πρὸς τ. πατέρα, Eph.3:14; by meton., πᾶν γόνυ for πᾶς, Rom.14:11 (LXX) Php.2:10 (cf. ἀνα-, συν-κάμπτω).† (AS)

2023.full: λαμπάς, -άδος, ἡ (λάμπω), [in LXX for לַפִּיד ;] a torch (frequently fed, like a lamp, with oil): Mat.25:1 ff., Jhn.18:3, Act.20:8, Rev.4:5 8:10.† (AS)

2024.full: λέπρα, -ας, ἡ (λεπρός), [in LXX for צָרַעַת ;] leprosy: Mat.8:3, Mrk.1:42, Luk.5:12-13† (AS)

2025.full: anything received, income , (Aeschulus Tragicus); λ. καὶ ἀνάλωμα receipt and expense, (Plato Philosophus): generally, gain, profit , Lat. lucrum, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; παντὸς ἥττων λήμματος unable to resist any temptation of gain , (Demosthenes Orator); often in plural, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

2027.lxx: in LXX: Gen.5:24 (לָקַח), Deu.27:17, al. (סוּג hi.), Sir.44:16, 2Ma.7:24, al
2027.full: μετα-τίθημι [in LXX: Gen.5:24 (לָקַח), Deu.27:17, al. (סוּג hi.), Sir.44:16, 2Ma.7:24, al ;] __1. to transfer to another place: with accusative, pass., Heb.11:5 (LXX); before εἰς, Act.7:16 __2. to change: with accusative, pass., Heb.7:12; before εἰς, figuratively, i.e. to make one thing a pretext for another, χάριν εἰς ἀσέλγειαν, Ju 4. Mid., to change oneself, pass over: before ἀπό and εἰς, Gal.1:6 (cf. 2Mac, l.with).† (AS)

2028.lxx: in LXX chiefly for הָלִלָה, הָלילָה
2028.full: μηδαμῶς (= μηδαμῆ, -δαμά, adv. fr. μηδαμός = μηδείς) [in LXX chiefly for הָלִלָה, הָלילָה ;] by no means, not at all. μ., Κύριε (sc. τοῦτο γένοιτο), Act.10:14 11:8.† (AS)

2029.full: μισθόω, -ῶ (μισθός) [in LXX (mid.) chiefly for שָׂכָר ;] to let out for hire. Mid., to hire: with accusative, Mat.20:1, 7.† (AS)

2030.full: νεανίας, -ου, ὁ (νεάν = νέος) [in LXX for נַעַר, בָּחוּר ;] a young man: Act.7:58 20:9 23:17-18.† (AS)

2031.full: οἷος, -α, -ον relat. pron., qualitative (related to ὅς as qualis to qui), what sort or manner of, such as, in NT usually without its correl. τοιοῦτος : Mat.24:21, Mrk.9:3, 2Co.12:20, 1Th.1:5, 2Ti.3:11, Rev.16:18; before τοιοῦτος, 1Co.15:48 15:2 2Co.10:11; id. redundant, Mrk.13:19; τ. αὑτὸν . . . σἷον, Php.1:30; οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι, elliptically, but it is not as though (RV), Rom.9:6.† (AS)

2033.full: πατέω, -ῶ [in LXX for דָּרַךְ, etc. ;] __1. intrans., to tread, walk: before ἐπάνω ὄφεων κ.τ.λ. (figuratively), Luk.10:19 (cf. Psa.91:13). __2. Trans., to tread on, trample: τ. ληνόν, Rev.14:20 19:15 (cf. Jdg.9:27, La 1:15, al.); of the desecration of Jerusalem by its enemies, Luk.21:24, Rev.11:2 (cf. κατα-, περι-, ἐν-περι-πατέω).† (AS)

2035.lxx: in LXX chiefly for רַב and cognate forms
2035.full: πλεῖστος, πλείων, see: πολύς. πολύς, πολλή, πολύ, [in LXX chiefly for רַב and cognate forms ;] __1. as adj., much, many, great, of number, space, degree, value, time, etc.: ἀριθμός, Act.11:21; ὄχλος, Mrk.5:24; θερισμός, Mat.9:37; χόρτος, Jhn.6:10; χρόνος, Mat.25:19; γογγυσμός, Jhn.7:12; πόνος, Col.4:13; δόξα, Mat.24:30; σιγή, Act.21:40; pl., προφῆται, Mat.13:17; ὄχλοι, Mat.4:25; δαιμόνια, Mrk.1:34; δυνάμεις, Mat.7:22, __2. As subst., pl. masc, πολλοί, many (persons): Mat.7:22, Mrk.2:2, al.; with genitive partit., Mat.3:7, Luk.1:16, al.; before ἐκ, Jhn.7:31, Act.17:12; with art., οἱ π., the many, Mat.24:12, Rom.12:5, 1Co.10:17, 33 2Co.2:17; opposite to ὁ εἶς (Lft., Notes, 291), Rom.5:15, 19; neut. pl., πολλά: Mat.13:3, Mrk.5:26, al.; accusative with adverbial force, Mrk.1:45, Rom.16:6 (Deiss., LAE, 317), 1Co.16:12, Jas.3:2, al.; neut. sing., πολύ: Luk.12:48; adverbially, Mrk.12:27, al.; πολλοῦ (genitive pret.), Mat.26:9; with compar. (Bl., §44, 5), π. σπουδαιότερον, 2Co.8:22; πολλῷ πλείους, Jhn.4:41. Compar., πλείων , neut., πλεῖον and πλέον (see WH, App., 151), pl., πλείονες, -ας, -α, contr., πλείους, -ω (cf. Mayser, 69), more, greater; __1. as adj.: Jhn.15:2, Act.18:2o, Heb.3:3; before παρά, Heb.11:4 (cf. Westc, in l. Was ΠΛΙΟΝΑ here a primitive error for ΗΔΙΟΝΑ ?); pi., Act.13:31, al.; with genitive compar., Mat.21:36; with num. (ἤ of comp. omitted), Act.4:22 24:11, al. __2. As subst., οἱ π., the greater number: Act.10:32 27:12, 1Co.10:5 15:6; also (Bl., §44, 3) others, more, the more: 2Co.2:6 4:15, Php.1:14; πλείονα, Luk.11:53; πλειον, πλέον, Mat.20:10, 2Ti.3:9; with genitive comp., Mk 12:43, Luk.21:3; π. Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε, Mat.12:41; adverbially, Act.4:17 20:9 24:4. __3. As adv., πλεῖον: before ἤ, Luk.9:13; with genitive comp., Mat.5:20; πλείω: with num., Mat.26:53. Superl., πλεῖστος, -η, -ον , __(a) prop., most: Mat.11:20 21:8; adverbially, τὸ π., 1Co.14:27; __(b) elative (M, Pr., 79), very great: ὄχλος π., Mrk.4:1. (AS)

2036.full: πολίτης, -ου, ὁ (πόλις), [in LXX chiefly for רֵעַ ;] __1. a citizen: with genitive loc., Luk.15:15, Act.21:39. __2. a fellow-citizen: with genitive of person(s), Luk.19:14, Heb.8:11" (LXX) .† (AS)

s: reflexive, to stick to, cleave to
2038.full: προσ-κολλάω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for דָּבַק ;] to glue to; pass., reflexive, to stick to, cleave to (Plat.): metaphorically (with dative, Jos.23:8, Sir.6:34 al.), before πρός, Mrk.10:7 (R, txt.), Eph.5:31 (LXX).† (AS)

2039.lxx: in LXX for קָרַב, נָגַשׁ, etc.
2039.full: προσ-πορεύομαι [in LXX for קָרַב, נָגַשׁ, etc. ;] to come near, approach: with dative of person(s), Mrk.10:35.† (AS)

2040.full: 1. to sprinkle , φάρμακα πάσσων laying salves upon a wound, (Iliad by Homer): —;with genitive partitive, πάσσε ἁλός sprinkle some salt, (Iliad by Homer) 2. to besprinkle , χρυσῶι, ῥόδοις π. τινά (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. metaphorically to embroider, broider , (Iliad by Homer); π. ἀέθλους to work battles in embroidery , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

2041.full: 1. of or belonging to one's father , Lat. patrius, (Pindar), etc. 2. = πατρικός, derived from one's fathers, hereditary , οἱπ. θεοί (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: —; τὰ πάτρια, Lat. instituta majorum, κατὰ τὰ πάτρια (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; rarely in singular, τὸ πάτριον παρείς neglecting the rule of our fathers , (Thucydides) Cf. πατρῷος. (ML)

s: to be confounded, greatly troubled, much distressed
2042.full: to throw all together into confusion, to confound, disturb, trouble , Lat. conturbare, (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;Pass., αἰθὴρ πόντῳ ξυντετάρακται air is confounded with sea, (Aeschulus Tragicus): to be thrown into confusion , of soldiers, (Thucydides); of social order, (Sophocles Tragicus); metaphorically of persons, to be confounded, greatly troubled, much distressed , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

2043.full: 1. a putting together, composition, combination , (Plato Philosophus); γραμμάτων συνθέσεις, i. e. syllables and words, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;also, of an author's composition , (Isocrates Orator) 2. metaphorically, like συνθεσία, an agreement, treaty , (Pindar) 3. Lat. synthesis was a suit of clothes , (Martialis Epigrammaticus Latinus); especially a loose gown , worn at dinner-parties, (Martialis Epigrammaticus Latinus) (ML)

s: to live daintily, luxuriously, to fare sumptuously
2044.lxx: in LXX: Neh.9:25 (עָדַן hithp.), Isa.66:11 (עָנַג hithp.), Sir.14:4 *
2044.full: τρυφάω, -ῶ (τρυφή), [in LXX: Neh.9:25 (עָדַן hithp.), Isa.66:11 (עָנַג hithp.), Sir.14:4 * ;] to live daintily, luxuriously, to fare sumptuously: Jas.5:5 (cf. ἐν-τρυφάω).† SYN.: σπαταλάω (which see), στρηνιάω (AS)

s: a body of men destined for service
2045.full: 1. a looking out, watch, guard , as a duty, (Herdotus Historicus); φρουρὰν ἄζηλον ὀχήσω shall keep unenviable watch , (Aeschulus Tragicus); φρουρὰ ὄμματος my watchful eye, (Sophocles Tragicus); φρουρᾶς ᾄδειν to sing while on guard , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. a prison , (Plato Philosophus) 3. of persons, a watch, guard, garrison , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; especially of frontier-posts , which were guarded in Attica by the περίπολοι, (Xenophon Historicus) 4. at Sparta, a body of men destined for service , φρουρὰν φαίνειν (see. φαίνω A. 1. 5). (ML)

2046.full: χωρίς adv., __1. separately, apart: Jhn.20:7. __2. As prep., with genitive, __(a) separate from, apart from, without (practically equiv. to ἄνευ; see Field, Notes, 103): Mat.13:34, Mrk.4:34, Luk.6:49, Jhn.1:3 15:5, Rom.3:21, 28 4:6 7:8-9 10:14, 1Co.4:8 11:11, 2Co.12:3, Eph.2:12, Php.2:14, 1Ti.2:8 5:21, Phm 14, Heb.4:15 7:7, 20 9:7, 18 9:22, 28 10:25 11:6, 40 12:8, 14 (οὗ χωρίς; see Bl., § 82, 3), Jas.2:18, 20 2:26; __(b) besides: Mat.14:21 15:38, 2Co.11:28.† (AS)

s: to break up, shift one's quarters
2048.full: 1. to yoke again , ἀναζευγνύναι τὸν στρατόν to move off the army, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀν. τὸ στρατόπεδον to break up the camp, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀν. τὰς νῆας to move Them back, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. absolute to break up, shift one's quarters , (Thucydides) (ML)

2049.lxx: in LXX for כְּסִיל, etc., chiefly in Wis. lit.
2049.full: ἀ-παίδευτος, -ον (παιδεύω), [in LXX for כְּסִיל, etc., chiefly in Wis. lit. ;] uninstructed, ignorant: 2Ti.2:23.† (AS)

s: to put of from oneself as a garment
2050.lxx: in LXX chiefly for נוּחַ hi.
2050.full: ἀπο-τίθημι [in LXX chiefly for נוּחַ hi. ;] to put off or aside; in NT always mid., __(a) to put of from oneself as a garment: τ. ἱμάτια, Act.7:58; metaphorically, in ethical sense, to put of, lay aside: Rom.13:12, Eph.4:22, 25, Col.3:8, Heb.12:1, Jas.1:21, 1Pe.2:1; __(b) to stow away, put: ἐν τ. φυλακῇ (MM, see word), Mat.14:3.† (AS)

2051.full: ἀσφάλεια, -ας, ἡ (ἀσφαλής), [in LXX for בָּטַח, etc. ;] __1. firmness. __2. certainty: Luk.1:4. __3. security: Act.5:23, 1Th.5:3. (In π. it is used as a law-term, proof, security; see MM, see word; M, Th., l.with)† (AS)

2052.full: ἄρωμα, -τος, τό [in LXX for בֶּשֶׂם ;] spice: Mrk.16:1, Luk.23:56 24:1, Jhn.19:40.† (AS)

2054.full: to draw out , (Iliad by Homer); so in Mid., ἐκσπασσαμένω ἔγχεα having drawn out their spears, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

2055.full: ἐλαιών, -ῶνος, ὁ (ἐλαία), [in LXX for זַיִת ;] olive-grove, olive-garden (so in FlJ and in π.; Deiss., BS, 209 ff.; MM, Exp., iii; M, Pr., 49, 69, 235): Luk.19:29 21:37 (WH, -ῶν; see their App., 158; Field, Notes, 73; El., § 10, 5; 33, 1; Thayer, see word), Act.1:12 (where EL, ll with, proposes the conjectural emendation ἐλαιῶν for -ῶνος).† (AS)

2056.full: 1. the elephant , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. the elephant's tusk, ivory , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

2057.lxx: in LXX: ἐξ ἐναντίας, for נֶגֶד, etc.; ἐναντίον, for פָּנִים etc.
2057.full: ἐν-αντίος, -α, -ον (ἀντίος, set against), [in LXX: ἐξ ἐναντίας, for נֶגֶד, etc.; ἐναντίον, for פָּנִים etc. ;] over against, opposite, contrary: ἄνεμος, Mat.14:24, Mrk.6:48, Act.27:4; ἐξ ἐναντίας (ellipse obscure, see Bl., § 44,1; Mozley, Psa.42:1-11), with genitive, Mrk.15:39. Metaphorical, opposed, hostile: 1Th.2:15, Act.26:9 28:17; ὁ ἐξ ἐ., Tit.2:8. Neuter., -ίον, adv., as prep. with genitive, before, in the presence of: Luk.1:6 20:26 24:19 Act.7:10 (ἔναντι, T), Act.8:32 (LXX).† (AS)

2058.lxx: in LXX: Lev.22:27, Num.32:19, al. (הָלְאָה), etc.
